newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea expects record rice harvest this year.
newsitem.headline: South Korea expects record rice harvest this year.

text.p: South Korea expects a record rice harvest this year of 5.07 million tonnes, up 8.0 percent on the 1995 harvest of 4.69 million tonnes, the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry said on Monday.
The harvest is expected to be 4.5 percent higher than the originally forecast 4.85 million tonnes, a ministry official said in a telephone interview.
"If there is no frost damage in the crop area it will be the biggest crop ever," he said.
The crop has been boosted by good weather this year.

In addition, there has been a sharp slowdown in the decline of land used for rice cultivation. The loss this year is projected at 6,000 hectares, leaving 1.05 million hectares. Last year 47,000 hectares were lost.
In 1995, rice paddy covered 1.056 million hectares, in 1994 1.103 million hectares and in 1993 1.136 million.

A nationwide survey last month indicated the yield from 10 acres (4 hectares) of rice paddy would reach a record average 483 kg (1,062 lb) this year, up 8.5 percent from 445 kg last year. The previous record was 481 kg in 1988.

The official said this year's harvest should ensure a balance of domestic supply and demand while maintaining rice stocks at an optimum level for next year. South Korea would not need to import any more than its World Trade Organisation quota of 76,961 tonnes next year.
This year, South Korea imported 64,136 tonnes of Chinese Japonica type rice under WTO Minimum Market Access rules.
The official said the latest forecast "will wipe out some worries, based on an expectation of low rice production, that we have to import additional rice next year to meet domestic demand".
Rice stockpiles had shrunk dramatically, despite an annual two percent drop in per capita rice consumption since the mid-1980s, the official said.
Stockpiles surged to 2.02 million tonnes in 1990 from 1.43 million tonnes in 1985, but dropped to 1.16 million tonnes in 1994 and 0.68 million tonnes in 1995.
